title: How 'Sunrise on the Reaping' Connects to 'The Hunger Games'
author: Megan McCluskey
body:
Warning: This post contains spoilers for Sunrise on the Reaping.

Twenty-four years before Katniss Everdeen volunteered as tribute to save her younger sister Prim from being reaped into the 74th Annual Hunger Games, her future District 12 mentor Haymitch Abernathy was forced to take part in his own Games. Given Haymitch was still alive at the start of The Hunger Games, we already knew he survived the 50th Games and was the victor of the infamous Second Quarter Quell, where twice the usual number of tributes were reaped. But in Sunrise on the Reaping, a new prequel film from director Francis Lawrence (The Hunger Games, The Long Walk) based on Suzanne Collins' 2025 novel of the same name, we get to see exactly how Haymitch's win played out. And it turns out it involved a lot of familiar faces from the original trilogy.

With Joseph Zada playing a teenage version of Woody Harrelson's Haymitch, Sunrise on the Reaping, now in theaters, follows our protagonist as he's ripped away from his family and girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), whisked off to the Capitol alongside fellow District 12 tributes Maysilee Donner (McKenna Grace), Wyatt Callow (Ben Wang), and Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), and made to take part in the slog of perverse rituals that accompany the Games each year. The story is chock-full of Easter eggs that recontextualize the events of The Hunger Games and its sequels by exposing how heavily the Capitol manipulated history and showing how the Second Rebellion was the culmination of decades of underground resistance rather than simply the result of a sudden uprising ignited by Katniss.

Let the games begin

On the morning of the Reaping, which happens to fall on Haymitch's birthday each year, he commiserates with his close friends and fellow potential tributes Asterid March (Grace Ackary) and Burdock Everdeen (Scot Greenan)—the couple we know as Katniss' future mother and father—over what's to come. Later, at the District 12 ceremony, Haymitch is introduced to cameraman and propagandist Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons playing a younger version of the late Philip Seymour Hoffman's Capitol insider), who eventually reveals himself as the rebel sympathizer we meet in the original trilogy.

Once in the Capitol, Haymitch meets past victors Beetee Latier (Kelvin Harrison Jr. as a younger Jeffrey Wright), Wiress (Maya Hawke as Amanda Plummer), and Mags Flanagan (Lili Taylor as Lynn Cohen), all of whom are once again reaped and made to participate in the Third Quarter Quell alongside Katniss (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta (Josh Hutcherson) in Catching Fire. After Haymitch makes a show of staring down and mockingly applauding President Coriolanus Snow (Ralph Fiennes as Donald Sutherland) in defiance in the wake of Louella's death at the tributes parade, Beetee sends his young son Ampert (Percy Daggs IV), who was also reaped as a tribute for the 50th Games, to begin recruiting Haymitch to take part in their secret plot to sabotage the Capitol from inside the Games arena. Wiress, Mags, and Plutarch are in on this plan as well.

Before the Games begin, Haymitch also makes the acquaintance of up-and-coming stylist Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning as a younger version of Elizabeth Banks' District 12 escort), who quickly takes a liking to his outspoken and scrappy nature.

May the odds be ever in your favor

Although Haymitch manages to successfully blow up the arena's underground water tank and flood its computer systems from within, the Capitol is able to regain control and cuts the TV footage in such a way that it erases any evidence of a rebel plot. After Haymitch ultimately wins the Games by using the arena's force field to deflect an axe thrown by Silka (Laura Marcus), his last remaining opponent, back at her, President Snow punishes Haymitch personally by humiliating him at the victor's ceremony and arranging for the deaths of his mother, his younger brother, and Lenore Dove. Realizing that Snow will never allow anyone he loves to live out their life in peace, Haymitch descends into a spiral of heavy drinking and self-hatred and deliberately distances himself from anyone in District 12 who still cares about him, including Burdock and Asterid.

However, a visit from Plutarch convinces him he needs to not fully give up and instead find a way to carry on in the hope that one day the right tributes will come along to finish what they started. This leads to an epilogue scene that jumps to a time well after the events of Mockingjay when an older Haymitch (Harrelson reprising the role) is finally living in peace alongside Katniss (Lawrence) and Peeta (Hutcherson). On his birthday, a day that previously would've marked another year of the Capitol selecting its tributes, Haymitch goes to visit the field where he used to meet Lenore Dove as she tended to her flock of geese, having finally fulfilled his promise to stop the sun from rising on another reaping.
